title: Measure your bio-age at home: Bryan Johnson's 7 free Bioage Fitness tests
summary: Bryan Johnson and the Blueprint clinical team outline seven free at-home fitness tests (push-ups, sit-rise, waist-to-height, grip strength, sit-and-reach, one-leg stand, reaction time) whose results are entered in the Don't Die app to get a biological age. He also points to Blueprint's paid blood panels, microplastics test and Speed of Aging for deeper baselines.

principles.text: Biological age can be estimated for free at home with seven simple fitness tests, entered into the Don't Die app.
principles.quote: Here are 7 free Bioage Fitness tests designed by the Blueprint clinical team that you can do at home.

principles.text: Waist-to-height ratio is a measure of body fat distribution and metabolic risk; smaller is better.
principles.quote: Assess body fat distribution, metabolic health and risk.

principles.text: Grip strength is tracked as a marker correlating with cardiovascular disease risk; higher is better.
principles.quote: Assess hand and forearm strength. Correlates with cardiovascular disease risk.

principles.text: The sit-rise test assesses flexibility, strength and balance; a score of 8 or more out of 10 is ideal.
principles.quote: The maximum score is 10. A score of 8 or more is considered ideal.

principles.text: Test endurance, balance and reaction speed: push-ups, one-leg stand with eyes shut, and best-of-five reaction time.
principles.quote: Hold this position as long as possible without touching the raised leg to the ground, using external support, or touching their other leg.

principles.text: For deeper baselines, use comprehensive blood and urine panels, microplastics screening and organ-system aging tests.
principles.quote: Test either 60 or 115 biomarkers with a comprehensive suite of blood and urine tests designed for deep analysis and insights
